title: H252 — Berry Phase Rate as Early-Warning Regime Shift Detector
rationale: Our current regime detection stack (VIX < 25 + SPY > 200MA) is reactive: it identifies a regime only after the price action has already moved. arXiv:2605.17117 proposes an unsupervised geometric approach using spectral embeddings of equity-index returns. The Berry Phase Rate — a quantum-mechanics-inspired observable extracted from the eigenstructure of rolling return covariance — achieves median OOS Cohen's d = 0.72 (95% CI [0.34, 1.18]) with 67% fewer false alarms per year than a supervised Random Forest (1.2 vs 3.6 false alarms/year). Crucially, the Berry Phase Rate is largely uncorrelated with classical signals (mean |ρ| ≈ 0.22), suggesting it captures a distinct risk dimension. This makes it a potential early-warning layer to complement our VIX+SPY composite rather than replace it. Implementation path: (1) replicate the spectral embedding on SPY daily returns (the paper provides code at github.com/willhammondhimself/qcml-geometric-sde); (2) compute Berry Phase Rate on a rolling 90-day window; (3) test as a binary early-warning signal (threshold: top quartile of Berry Phase Rate = elevated regime-shift risk); (4) evaluate: does adding Berry Phase Rate to the H249 regime signal improve OOS performance vs H249 alone? If Berry Phase Rate is already elevated, delay regime-switch trades by 5 days (wait for confirmation). Confirm gate: The Berry Phase Rate signal must add statistically significant predictive power for regime transitions beyond VIX + SPY 200MA (measured by AUC on labeled crisis windows 2000–2026: 17 events from the paper).
